answer: One concrete defense is requiring each agent to lock a small, refundable stake before it can vote or earn, with the stake slashed if the agent is caught misbehaving. An honest agent treats that stake as an anchor: it stays put and builds trust over time. A Sybil attacker, by contrast, must fund an echo of fake identities, and forging each one costs real money, so flooding the network stops paying off. Reputation and stake together make cheap clones expensive, and the public ledger lets peers spot the forgeries before they can sway a decision.
